fit.verdict: Weakest of the three Mercury roles. Wrong surface area (packaging-led vs. campaign/editorial) and no agency/fashion/elevated-consumer pedigree. AI POV is a standout but it is one bullet, not the job.

criteria.name: Portfolio: mastery of type/layout/color/composition across brand contexts
criteria.note: 1,331 portfolio images + editorial format work broadens it, but still packaging-weighted vs. Mercury's campaign/editorial bar.

criteria.name: High-craft background (agency/fashion/elevated consumer/design-forward tech)
criteria.note: Small-business + CPG sales. No pedigree signal.

criteria.name: 7-10+ yrs brand design
criteria.note: Years met; 'brand design' specifically is partial.

criteria.name: Brand systems at scale / stewarded through growth
criteria.note: Style Registry, multi-SKU frameworks, a brand rebuilt in production.

criteria.name: Figma + design system ownership
criteria.note: Builds systems in code, not Figma.

criteria.name: Staff-level operating (autonomy, influence, shapes a team's output)
criteria.note: Founder autonomy + solo-shipped a full product; not org-context.

criteria.name: AI POV in high-craft design
criteria.note: Production AI pipelines, provider routing, fine-tuning, explicit 'where AI does not belong' rules.

strengths: Genuine, documented POV on AI in the creative process (matches a dedicated JD bullet)
Systems thinking — zone-based template frameworks, Style Registry governance
15 years creative; numeric experience bar met
gaps: No agency / fashion / elevated-consumer / design-forward-tech pedigree
Portfolio is packaging/product-render led, not campaign/web/social/editorial
No track record mentoring IC3/IC4 designers

improvementPlan.summary: The score is dragged down by four things: a packaging-weighted portfolio, no agency pedigree, no Figma system ownership, and no visible mentoring. Three of the four are fixable in 4-8 weeks using assets Paintbrush already has — a 1,331-piece body of client work, a code-level design system, a production AI pipeline, and years of art-directing contractors. Executed, this moves from ~4.5 (long shot) to ~6.2 (borderline-apply).

actions.do: Cut 3 tight editorial/campaign case studies from the existing Behance library — a typographic system, a campaign with layout range, and one motion/social set — presented as problem → system → crops, not as a gallery dump.
actions.why: The portfolio criterion carries the most weight (25%) and the raw material already exists; the gap is packaging framing, not missing work. Reframed range is the single biggest lever on this role.
actions.leverages: 1,331 Behance pieces + the what-if-it-worked editorial format breakdowns + the Style Registry as the 'system' narrative

actions.do: Rebuild one packaging system as a published Figma library — components, variants, tokens, and a short usage doc — mirroring the zone-based template system currently only in code.
actions.why: The JD explicitly asks for Figma proficiency and design-system ownership; the thinking is already done, it just isn't in the tool they screen on.
actions.leverages: The multi-SKU zone template framework and Style Registry governance already built in the Paintbrush codebase

actions.do: Publish the AI-in-craft methodology as a written POV piece on the Paintbrush blog / Behance — the label generator, provider routing, fine-tuning on past label sets, and the 'never render headline text in the image model' rule as a stated philosophy.
actions.why: The JD wants 'conviction and language to articulate what makes something great' plus a real AI point of view. A written POV is the artifact that proves both, and it is a differentiator no other applicant will have.
actions.leverages: The prompt-system docs, the LLM provider router, the Magnific compositing guide, and the existing blog infrastructure
actions.lifts: Aesthetic point of view / AI POV credibility (supports the portfolio and staff-level read)

actions.do: Write one 'how I run design review' reference doc and add a concrete résumé line about art-directing contract photographers/illustrators and running client design crits.
actions.why: Mentoring reads as zero right now, but years of directing contractors and revising client work is real craft-leadership evidence — it just isn't written down.
actions.leverages: Retainer client work where Paintbrush directed external creatives and ran revision rounds

actions.do: Get one referral or portfolio review from someone in an agency / elevated-consumer / design-forward-tech environment — reach out to past beverage/supplement clients who work with agencies, or design-community contacts.
actions.why: Pedigree is the hardest gap to close on paper; a credible voice vouching for craft is the realistic substitute and also lifts the 'influence without authority' read.
actions.leverages: The existing multi-industry client network and past AMA / design-community connections

nextAction: Hold on applying. Work the improvement plan (3 editorial case studies + a Figma library + a written AI-craft POV) — projected ~6.2 once done, then apply.

history.event: Logged and fit-scored ~4.5/10 against the fuller paintbrush codebase evidence
